region: Riverhead · North Fork of Long Island, New York
about: RGNY stands for Rivero González New York, the North Fork estate of a Mexican winegrowing family who planted their first vines in Parras, Coahuila, in 1998. About twenty years later they bought the former Martha Clara Vineyards on Sound Avenue in Riverhead, once known for its hayrides and petting zoo, and reopened it as RGNY in 2019. The family now farms roughly 88 acres of vines there, between Long Island Sound and Peconic Bay, and has turned the property into a quieter, wine-focused estate.

This is the estate’s serious, Bordeaux-style white, and a limited release. The fruit comes from the warmest part of the vineyard, its southernmost tip, which gives deeper and more textured wine than the brighter Scielo Sauvignon Blanc. It is fermented and aged in French oak, half of it new, for eleven months, with the lees stirred to build richness. Winemaker Jonathan Bomberg has described the approach as drawing on both the Loire and Bordeaux, and calls it one of his favourite wines to make.

Fuller in body than most North Fork whites, it shows light floral and ripe yellow-apple notes with a honeyed edge, and a creamy, gently toasty texture from the barrels. The winery suggests serving it only lightly chilled and says it can age three to five years, as nutty notes emerge to balance the oak. It is a natural partner for lobster or a basil pesto pasta.
facts: Southernmost (warmest) block of the RGNY estate, North Fork
11 months in French oak, 50% new, with lees stirring
